record.file_problem: Table 1 is referenced as the experiment results, but its contents and numerical values are absent from the supplied text; the surrounding paper is readable.
record.tranche_reason: It reports outcomes from sweeps over hidden-layer width and L1 regularization that bear on double-descent behavior, using a two-layer MNIST network rather than the original studies’ methods and settings.
record.gate_note: The paper explicitly reports sparse double descent across the tested widths, many ascents and descents as width decreases, and an invariant location of minima with respect to the regularization coefficient. Table 1 is not available, so no numerical results can be extracted.
record.test_reason: The only reported results are prose descriptions of test performance along an L1-sparsity axis ('sparse double descent'), at six hidden widths of a two-layer MNIST MLP. Sparsity is not an axis any version names; V1 is size, V2 epochs, V3 samples. The study gives no width-wise test-error curve and no interpolation threshold. It gives no noise manipulation and no check of whether tuned regularization removes a peak. Table 1, the sole results artifact, is empty in the text, so no number or metric can be read. These findings belong under fits_no_version, not as a test of any version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The author reports that varying the L1 coefficient yields a version of sparse double descent at every tested width. The author reports more ascents and descents as width shrinks. The minima location is reported as invariant to α, suggested to mean sparse double descent is independent of layer width. The author calls for validation on more complex models and datasets. The record's phrase 'width changes can yield many ascents and descents' overstates it; the text does not establish a width-axis curve.
record.recipe_differences: Uses a two-layer ReLU MLP trained on MNIST and varies hidden representation dimension and L1 regularization; it does not reproduce the original studies’ reported size, epoch, or sample-size experiments.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported behavior is examined across intermediate-layer widths and L1 regularization coefficients; the authors report the minima location is invariant with respect to α.

fits_no_version.finding: For every tested width (5–100 hidden units), test performance along increasing L1 strength shows a sparse double descent, per prose only.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sparse double descent: as L1-induced sparsity increases, test performance worsens, improves, then worsens near full sparsity.

fits_no_version.finding: More ascents and descents appear at smaller widths, and the minima location is reported as invariant to α.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The number of descents along the sparsity axis depends on hidden width; minima location is independent of the regularization coefficient.

record.problems: The central results table is unavailable in the supplied text, leaving no numerical values or exact metric to check. The reported experiments use one dataset and a specific two-layer architecture; uncertainty estimates and controls are not stated.
record.rows_left_out: No additional numerical rows could be extracted because Table 1 is absent from the supplied text. The prose reports the width sweep and α-related findings only in aggregate.

untested.parts: No test-error curve over model width and no interpolation threshold are reported.
Only a two-layer MLP is used; LASSO is mentioned as motivation but no results are given.
No label-noise manipulation, no mechanism test, and no optimal-regularization check. Multiple ascents are reported only along the sparsity axis, in prose.
No re-expression in effective parameters, though Curth et al. is cited as motivation.

missing.what: Contents of Table 1 (per-width, per-α performance values and the metric used); the only quantitative evidence in the paper.
missing.versions: none directly; needed to check R1–R3

record.verdict_notes: This is a 3-page note with a single experiment described in three sentences, and the results table is blank in the text. The record's V1 limits_scope and V6 supports labels were removed because no row measures what those versions name and no value is readable. The study is not an original source.

versions.untested_parts: The reported width sweep does not identify an interpolation threshold or establish that the reported changes are specifically test error.
Changing the number of training samples near an interpolation threshold.
Double descent across model classes beyond the studied two-layer neural network.
A single effective-complexity measure predicting peak location across axes.

Whether noise or variance drives the peak, and whether optimally tuned regularization removes it. The paper reports multiple ascents and descents with width but does not test those mechanisms or optimal tuning.
Re-expressing results using an effective parameter count and testing whether the second descent becomes an ordinary U-shaped curve.

rows.subject: two-layer multilayer perceptron with ReLU non-linearity
rows.measure: Performance trend; exact metric is not stated in the available text.
rows.value: The paper reports many ascents and descents as the number of intermediate neurons decreases; numerical values are not available.
rows.note: The paper reports this pattern across the width sweep, but the missing table prevents identifying individual width-specific values or the exact metric.
rows.check: The sentence 'many ascents and descents as we decrease the number of intermediate neurons' is ambiguous. Most plausibly it means smaller widths show more ups and downs along the α/sparsity curve, not a model-wise width curve. The metric is unstated, there are no values (Table 1 is empty), and no interpolation threshold is identified. It cannot be read as model-wise double descent (V1). Nor is it shown to be V6-style multiple peaks tied to noise or variance. The earlier link to V1/V6 with state 'partial' is unsupported.
